chapter: First bands and the road in the South
title: Joining Eagle Eye Shields in Jacksonville
summary: Edmond Hall went to pianist-leader Eagle Eye Shields, recommended Cootie, and his father arranged for his Jacksonville partner to look after him.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: They played by ear. They didn't have no music. And Edmund Hall left the Pensacola Jazz Band, and he went to Florida to join another band by the name of Eagle Eye Shields.

And he told him about me. So they got in touch with my father. My father's partner in the gambling house business happened to live in Jacksonville, Florida. So he told them he would have to talk to his partner about it first. To see if the partner would take care of me. So the partner said yes, that he would look after me. And so that's how I got a chance to leave home. To go down there to play with Eagle Eye Shields. His was the first band I ever played with.
